course.title.back: Southeast Asia from Time to Time
course.title.note: "Dari masa ke masa" (from time to time) is the usual Indonesian way to say "through time". The interface (id.json's preview banner and preview page) still calls the course "Southeast Asia Through Time": decide which name to use and change the other.

course.description.source: Investigate how people in Southeast Asia lived, connected across seas, faced changing power, built new nations, and preserve their histories. Explore real objects, archives, places, photographs, and different points of view.
course.description.back: Investigate how people in Southeast Asia lived, were connected by sea, faced changing power, built new nations, and look after their history. Explore objects, archives, places, photos and different points of view, all of them real.
course.description.note: "Real" (nyata) moved to the end of the sentence so it covers all five things, as in the English.

sections.0.question.source: What do objects and places tell us about early lives and trade by sea?
sections.0.question.back: What do objects and places tell about early life and trade by sea?

sections.0.description.source: Study a pot from Ban Chiang, old boat planks from Butuan and maps of Melaka, and learn to tell what a source shows from what we guess.
sections.0.description.back: Study a pot from Ban Chiang, old boat planks from Butuan and maps of Melaka, then learn to tell what a source shows from what we guess.

sections.1.question.source: Who gained, who worked, and who challenged unfair rules?
sections.1.question.back: Who profited, who worked, and who opposed rules that were not fair?

sections.1.description.source: Follow nutmeg from Banda, rubber from Malaya and letters from Kartini, and ask whose story each source tells.
sections.1.description.back: Follow the trail of nutmeg from Banda, rubber from Malaya and Kartini's letters, then ask whose story each source tells.

sections.2.question.source: How did war and independence change different communities?
sections.2.question.back: How did war and independence change different communities?

sections.2.description.source: See how war changed daily life in Singapore, compare how Indonesia and Malaya became independent, and look at how Timor-Leste rebuilt its schools.
sections.2.description.back: See how war changed daily life in Singapore, compare Indonesia's and Malaya's paths to independence, and see how Timor-Leste rebuilt its schools.
sections.2.description.note: Section 3 is translated by the other translator's lessons (7–9): check these words match their lesson titles.

sections.3.question.source: How do people choose which stories to keep and share?
sections.3.question.back: How do people choose which stories are kept and shared?

sections.3.description.source: Visit the port of Hội An and the temple of Borobudur, then plan a small exhibition that tells a shared history fairly.
sections.3.description.back: Visit the port of Hội An and the temple of Borobudur, then plan a small exhibition that tells a shared history fairly.
sections.3.description.note: "Temple" → "candi", the Indonesian word for Borobudur and other old Hindu-Buddhist temples.

practiceOptions.3.back: I practised another way (silently, with sign language, or in writing)
